title: Settlement and Recoveries on Keyturn Host Protection Plan Claims
content:
Money accepted on a claim under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan reaches the host through their payout account and never by any other route, and it is released within the plan's payment period counted in business days from the day the claim was accepted.

### No claim is paid twice

A claim that has already been paid in full is not paid again, so where a payment record already stands against the same accepted claim and that payment was not itself reversed, the request is a duplicate and no further money moves. What settles it is the payment records standing against that same accepted claim, read before any money is released, and not the host's recollection of whether they were paid.

### Part payments

Part payments are allowed where a claim settles in stages, and several part payments against one claim are allowed as long as their total stays inside what was accepted; each carries its own date so that two part payments of the same amount stay separable.

### Recoveries

Money recovered from a guest or a third party clears the host's liability first and only then reduces what the marketplace has paid out, and the marketplace pursues recovery for the plan's pursuit period before closing it whatever the prospects. A recovery received after the claim is closed is still applied to the host's liability, because a closed claim does not extinguish a debt already recovered.

### A hold on the payout account

Where the host's payout account is on hold no claim money is released, since the hold exists precisely to stop money leaving while something is unresolved, and the host is told which hold is blocking it rather than simply that payment is delayed. The state of the account is read from the host's own payout account record before money is released, and only an account in the active state admits a release.

### Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

A hypothetical claim accepted at 2400 settles in two stages of 1500 and 900. Both stand against the same claim, each with its own date, and their total is inside what was accepted. A third request for 900 on the same claim, with neither earlier payment reversed, moves no further money.
